text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. One common type is supervised learning, where the computer uses labeled examples to understand patterns. These examples, called training data, consist of inputs paired with correct outputs. For instance, you might show a model thousands of pictures of cats and dogs, each labeled correctly. The model studies these examples to build an internal rule, or model, that can then make predictions on new, unseen pictures. After training, we test the model’s accuracy by checking how often its predictions match the true answers. A higher accuracy means the model has learned the patterns well, making it reliable for future real-world tasks.
